answer: Distinct-Site Binding: an identity must anchor to a physical location whose readings (RF noise floor, power-line hum, ambient light) wander unpredictably and cross-check against a second sensor at the same site. A remote operator can spoof one sensor feed cheaply, but matching two independently drifting streams requires co-located hardware behind a vault the attacker cannot clone from a distance. Forging each extra identity therefore costs one full installed sensor package plus upkeep at a distinct ridge-separated site, turning a mass clone into mass construction.
